notes: mc GEOGRAPHY (10-Q 2026-09-30, by user location, 9M2026): North America 62.8% of revenue (7,455 of 11,863; US = 95% of NA, so ~60% US), EMEA 25.3%, Asia Pacific and other 11.8%. Growth 9M26 vs 9M25: NA +22%, EMEA +21%, APAC +26%. Property and equipment net (2,145): NA 66%, EMEA 22%, APAC 12%; US = 84% of NA. Sources pf_10q_20261028, pf_10k_20260129. No China or Taiwan breakout is disclosed (APAC is one line); no hardware supply chain disclosed.

mc EXPOSURE export controls/sanctions/FCPA: 10-K risk factor (pf_10k_20260129) names Russia/Belarus sanctions and possible wider restrictions; no revenue share disclosed, so any sizing is hypothesis (non-US revenue is ~40%: EMEA 25% + APAC 12%, an upper bound of what international disruption could touch).

mc EXPOSURE tariffs: 10-K says ServiceNow pays customs tariffs in certain cases on imports for its operations (data center hardware); no amount disclosed, hypothesis only; a software subscription business, impact expected small but unsized.

mc EXPOSURE US federal / DOJ: 10-Q 2026-09-30 note (pf_10q_20261028): internal investigation on hiring of the former US Army CIO as Head of Global Public Sector (2023); DOJ opened its own investigation and requested documents; company cannot predict timing or outcome. Federal business is concentrated in a small number of distributors/resellers (10-K risk factor); debarment risk listed; share of revenue from US federal not found in this lane (gap).

mc EXPOSURE Middle East deal delays: press (mc_yahoo_q1, search excerpt, not primary) attributes part of the Q1 2026 stock drop to Middle East deal delays and Armis margin pressure; unsized, treat as lead until confirmed in call transcript (documents lane).
mc EXPOSURE AI disruption of seat-based IT service workflows: press (mc_invezz_jul) cites investor worry that AI agents reduce employees handling ITSM tickets; opinion, hypothesis, not sized here.

mc EXPOSURE data residency / local-partner rules and antitrust: generic risk factors in 10-K, no sizing. Moveworks antitrust review (DOJ second request, 2025 press) ended with closing on 2025-12-15 per 10-Q; no 2026 DOJ merger challenge found in search.

mc NEWS 2025-12-15 to 2026-04-20: Moveworks acquisition closed 2025-12-15 (10-Q note), Veza closed 2026-03-02 for about $1.2bn, Armis closed 2026-04-20 for preliminary consideration of about $7.6bn in cash (press says $7.75bn headline); nine-month cash paid for business combinations $9,167m (10-Q cash flow). Five other acquisitions for $612m in 9M26.

mc NEWS 2026-05-15: 8-K (mc_8k_20260515): $4.0bn of five series of senior unsecured notes issued May 2026 (net $3.9bn) to repay the $4.0bn term loan drawn for Armis; total senior notes now $5.5bn (incl. $1.5bn 1.40% 2030 notes), fair value $5.1bn at 2026-09-30 (10-Q).
mc NEWS 2026-04-23: press (mc_yahoo_q1) reports stock fell about 17% after Q1 2026 results on margin fears from Armis despite beat; press only, approximate.
mc NEWS 2026-02/05 8-Ks: 2026-02-11 (Item 5.02, officer/director change), 2026-02-17 (7.01), 2026-05-22 (5.02, 5.07 annual meeting results): not read in detail, no material event identified; gap.
